members.text:
## Review policy

Every change to shared rules needs a second reviewer before it lands, and the reviewer must not be the author.

members.name: review_body_v2
members.text:
## Review policy (revised)

Every change to shared rules needs a second reviewer before it lands, the reviewer must not be the author, and the review must be recorded against the exact revision it covers.

says: Alice binds her device key, authors a personal Instructions source (revision one, whose body digest the owner computes) and selects revision one in her personal Instructions position. She opens a link to her working conversation, composes a first preparation for delivery on it (basis scoped to her personal layer alone), delivers its body to the current recipient and observes the delivery: the inventory names revision one's unit and body. Later she authors revision two of the same source against the head revision one left, re-pins her position to revision two against the position's head (the digest of the collection her first change stored), and composes a second preparation for the same recipient whose basis now also scopes a repository layer alongside her personal one (a scope change from the first preparation): it names the position's new head and revision two's body. She then switches that entry off, and composes a third preparation over the same two scopes but with an explicit order preferring her personal layer over the repository one — the reverse of the repository-before-personal default the second preparation's unstated order applied (an order change from the second preparation): it names the position's newest head and holds the same source, member and revision two as disabled, with no body. Each preparation mints its own unit id; a unit is followed across preparations by its source, member and revision. Observing the first preparation after all three changes — the revision, the scope and the order — returns the same delivery observation as before, naming revision one, and writes nothing: the changes reached only the preparations composed after them. What must not happen: a recomposition rewriting the first preparation, the recipient's delivered inventory or the revision, scope or order it was composed under, or a change to the position writing the source itself — revision two moves the source's own head only through its own admission.
